results.output_text:
When generating text one word at a time, the computer usually spends a lot of time setting up the math for each new token. This setup process, known as kernel launch overhead, can be slower than the actual calculation itself. CUDA graphs solve this by recording the entire sequence of operations once and then replaying them like a pre-recorded video! This eliminates the repetitive setup work, allowing the GPU to focus purely on crunching numbers for each new word.

Meanwhile, the model needs to remember everything it has generated so far to keep the conversation coherent. This memory is stored in the Key-Value (KV) cache, which grows larger
